key_insight: SequenTx couples a virtual-cell model of dynamic cellular state transitions with reinforcement learning to design sequential drug regimens that proactively steer tumor evolution and reduce therapy-induced resistance.
problem_solved: Provides a computational strategy to navigate and control therapy-driven tumour evolution by anticipating cellular state changes and optimizing adaptive, time-varying treatment sequences.
method: Build a virtual-cell-inspired model that represents tumour heterogeneity as dynamic state transitions between cellular phenotypes.
Use reinforcement learning to search for optimal sequential drug policies that minimize tumour burden and delay or prevent resistance.
Evaluate candidate policies in simulated evolving tumour landscapes to compare adaptive sequences vs static or heuristic regimens.
impact: Demonstrates how combining mechanistic state models with RL addresses non-stationary control problems in biology; offers a transferable framework and experimental benchmark for ML researchers working on adaptive decision-making under shifting distributions.
visual_elements: Pipeline diagram: virtual-cell model → RL agent → simulated treatment rollout (clear arrows showing data flow).
State-transition network: nodes = cellular phenotypes, edges = transition probabilities influenced by drugs (iconography for drugs and resistant states).
Time-series comparison: tumour burden or resistant-population curves under SequenTx vs static policies.
Policy heatmap or decision timeline: which drug chosen across cellular-state space or over treatment cycles.
paper_title: Reinforcement learning-based design of sequential drug treatment targeting the evolving tumour landscape with SequenTx
paper_authors: Xiaohan Chen, Yue Deng, Xingbo Yang, Ying Zhang, Yuting Huang
